extracted.intended_audience: prospective students, prospective faculty, alumni, and members of the public seeking information about the UNC Hussman School of Journalism and Media
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional 'About' page describing mission, programs, enrollment, accreditation, campus visit information, and public accountability for a university journalism school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — prepare students to ignite the public conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: UNC Hussman School of Journalism and Media’s mission is to prepare students to ignite the public conversation in our state, the nation and the world, and to understand the role of communication in fostering democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission frames curricular and program decisions and suggests evaluative emphasis on students' ability to engage public discourse and understand communication's democratic role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum relevance and skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a revamped curriculum, students learn the skills to succeed in a dynamic media environment whether pursuing careers in journalism, advertising, public relations or other communications fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of the program should consider whether the curriculum equips students with contemporary, practical skills for changing media careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program breadth and degree offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: The school offers bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral degrees, and administers a variety of professional development and distance-learning programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments may account for the availability of undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, professional development, and online/distance options as part of program robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized focus programs and honors opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduate areas of study include advertising/public relations and journalism with focus programs in business communication, fashion communication and marketing, health communication and marketing, political communication and sports communication. A UNC Hussman Honors Program is also available to selected seniors pursuing research or creative projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality measures can include the presence and strength of focus tracks and honors pathways that support specialization and student research/creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACEJMC accreditation status and periodic review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Accrediting Council for Education in Journalism and Mass Communication (ACEJMC) is the national organization that evaluates journalism and mass communication programs. All accredited programs are reviewed every six years. UNC Hussman has been accredited since 1958.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation is an explicit quality standard; documentation should include dates of self-study, site visits, provisional or full reaccreditation decisions, and adherence to ACEJMC review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACEJMC self-study and site-visit process (including diversity/inclusiveness review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The accreditation process includes an extensive self-study conducted the year prior to a site visit. The school’s most recent self-study was completed and submitted to ACEJMC in September 2020 and subsequently updated ... ACEJMC voted in April 2022 to provisionally reaccredit UNC Hussman and then revisited the school in January 2024 to evaluate progress toward the accrediting body’s Diversity and Inclusiveness standard. In May 2024, ACEJMC voted unanimously to fully reaccredit the UNC Hussman School of Journalism and Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important evaluative criteria include the quality of the self-study, responsiveness during follow-up visits, and progress toward specific ACEJMC standards such as Diversity and Inclusiveness; accreditation decisions (provisional → full) and timelines are key evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accreditation (SACSCOC) for degree-granting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate, master’s, education specialist and doctoral degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional accreditation status and contact information for the commission serve as baseline legitimacy for the school's degree programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accountability via graduation and retention rates
rubrics_metrics.description: View the Graduation and Retention Rates for the UNC Hussman School of Journalism and Media by entering year. (Last updated July 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduation and retention statistics are explicit public metrics used to assess program outcomes and institutional accountability; up-to-date reporting is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment figures as descriptive metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: 1,288 Undergraduates enrolled in our two areas of study; 109 Graduates enrolled in our full-time programs. Enrollment includes about 1,200 undergraduate and more than 100 graduate students in addition to professional development and distance education students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment counts are presented as measures of program scale and can be used alongside outcome metrics to evaluate program capacity and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus location and visitability as part of student experience
rubrics_metrics.description: UNC Hussman is located on the historic Polk Place quad at the nation’s first public university — just a short distance from Carolina’s iconic Old Well. Chapel Hill ... offers a vibrant and charming setting to live and learn. Plan Your Visit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site's emphasis on location and visit information implies that campus setting and opportunities to visit are factors in evaluating student experience and fit.
